record.paper_title: Developments, Applications and Open Problems in Fixed Point Theory
record.original_question: A Banach space X is super-reflexive when no non-reflexive Banach space is finitely representable in X; finite representability here means that there is a number lambda > 1 such that every finite-dimensional subspace of the represented space embeds isomorphically into X with distortion bounded by lambda. Does every super-reflexive Banach space have the fixed point property, meaning that every nonempty closed bounded convex subset K of X has a fixed point for each nonexpansive self-map T: K -> K?

evidence.quote: A normed linear space X is considered finitely representable in another normed linear space Y if there exists a number lambda > 1 such that for each finite-dimensional subspace X_n of X, there exists an isomorphism T_n from X_n to Y satisfying lambda^-1 ||x|| <= ||T_n(x)|| <= lambda ||x|| if x in X_n. A super-reflexive Banach space is a Banach space X such that no non-reflexive Banach space can be finitely representable in X.
An intriguing unresolved question in this context is: Does every super-reflexive Banach space possess the FPP?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Definitions. Let X and Y be normed linear spaces. We say X is finitely representable in Y if there exists λ > 1 such that for every finite-dimensional subspace X_n ⊂ X there exists a linear isomorphism T_n : X_n → Y satisfying λ^{-1}‖x‖ ≤ ‖T_n x‖ ≤ λ‖x‖ for every x ∈ X_n. A Banach space X is called super-reflexive if no non-reflexive Banach space is finitely representable in X.

A Banach space X is said to have the fixed point property (FPP) for nonexpansive mappings if for every nonempty closed bounded convex subset K ⊂ X and every map T : K → K satisfying ‖T x − T y‖ ≤ ‖x − y‖ for all x, y ∈ K, there exists a point p ∈ K with T p = p.

Question. Does every super-reflexive Banach space have the fixed point property for nonexpansive mappings?

artifact.status_search_result: Whether every super-reflexive Banach space has the fixed point property for nonexpansive self-maps of closed bounded convex sets is a well-known open problem in metric fixed point theory. Partial results exist (e.g., super-reflexive spaces have the FPP for isometries, and FPP holds under additional geometric conditions such as normal structure or property (Sm)), but the general question remains unresolved as of recent surveys and papers.

status_evidence.title: Towards the fixed point property for superreflexive spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Paper devoted to progress toward establishing FPP for super-reflexive Banach spaces, indicating the problem is not fully resolved.
status_evidence.claim: The FPP for super-reflexive Banach spaces is an active, unresolved problem.

status_evidence.title: On the Fixed Point Property in Reflexive Banach Spaces (2025)
status_evidence.snippet: Recent arXiv paper discussing the still-open status of the FPP for reflexive (and super-reflexive) Banach spaces.
status_evidence.claim: As of 2025 the FPP question for reflexive/super-reflexive spaces is still being investigated.

status_evidence.title: Fixed Point Property in Banach spaces (survey slides)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of FPP in Banach spaces listing the super-reflexive case as an open problem.
status_evidence.claim: Survey lists the super-reflexive FPP question among open problems.
